experiment: triplet/contrastive on faces, target = normalized like/view (per-post e_rate)
interpretation: Pipeline clean: breaking the e_rate label collapses the readout to ~0 (no structural leak).
Triplet/contrastive objective contributes NOTHING: real target 0.289 == shuffled-encoder-target 0.297.
The ~0.29 signal comes entirely from a linear readout on pretrained CLIP face features, not from metric learning.
It is NOT facial beauty (beauty vs e_rate = 0.006); the full CLIP embedding captures photo style/quality/age/demographics.

Consistent with the whole investigation: face pixels weakly predict per-view engagement (~0.24-0.29), driven by non-beauty visual factors; contrastive training does not improve on a simple CLIP readout.
